intent: To illustrate the extremely thin profit margins typical in grocery retail businesses.

basis.note: profit-margin row; unit is percent; relative_value is 0.03

units.visual_evidence_rule: A label, legend, or annotation must show the profit margin as 3% (or 3 percent).
units.temporal_anchor: The clause stating 'you might manage a profit margin of 3%'.
units.reviewer_question: Should the exact 3% profit margin be required, or is a visual-only 3% slice enough?

units.meaning: The remainder of the ring is 97%, so the profit margin is only a small slice of the whole.

basis.note: ring-rest row; unit is percent; source_type is estimated
profit-margin row; used to establish the 3% slice in the same composition

accepted_routes: The remainder of the ring is 97%
97% of the ring is not profit margin
The rest of the donut is 97%
units.visual_evidence_rule: The donut/ring must visibly include a 97% remainder segment, or the remaining area must be labeled/legend-ed as 97%.
units.temporal_anchor: The same margin clause or the donut reveal that completes the ring after the 3% slice appears.
units.reviewer_question: Is the 97% remainder required as an explicit fact, or is it optional visual context?

units.meaning: The remainder is about 32.3 times the profit margin.
accepted_routes: The remainder is about 32 times the profit margin
The non-margin remainder is about 32.3 times the margin
Profit margin is about 1/32 of the remainder
units.visual_evidence_rule: A viewer must be able to see the large remainder vs tiny margin contrast; an annotation or label should communicate the ~32× ratio if this unit is required.
units.temporal_anchor: A contrast/summary clause after the 3% margin statement.
units.reviewer_question: Is the derived ~32× ratio required, optional, or too interpretive?

units.meaning: The gap between the 97% remainder and the 3% profit margin is 94 percentage points.
accepted_routes: The gap between remainder and margin is 94 percentage points
The remainder exceeds the margin by 94 percentage points
There is a 94 pp gap between the 97% remainder and 3% margin
units.visual_evidence_rule: A chart annotation or label should show the 97% vs 3% contrast and/or the 94 percentage-point gap.
units.temporal_anchor: A contrast/summary clause after the 3% margin statement.
units.reviewer_question: Is the derived 94-percentage-point gap required, optional, or unnecessary?

optional_valid: Profit margin can also be expressed as relative_value 0.03 (3/100).
The remainder row is marked source_type estimated; this provenance can be mentioned but is not a core data claim.
The profit margin is a tiny minority of the ring, i.e., 3% of the whole.
unsupported_to_avoid: Causal claim that one mistake or bad shelf arrangement wipes out all profit; the table does not quantify loss events.
Extrapolation that all grocery retailers have exactly a 3% profit margin; the table gives one clip-level value.
Calling the 97% remainder 'costs', 'expenses', or 'loss'; the table only labels it remainder of the ring.
Adding a revenue/sales denominator (e.g., 3% of revenue) unless the chart explicitly labels it as such.
Deriving a dollar example such as $3 profit on $100 in sales; no dollar amount is in the table.
notes: Core required content is the 3% profit margin; the 97% remainder and derived ratio/gap are valid but may be optional depending on whether the chart explicitly labels them. Avoid causal, extrapolative, or unspecified-denominator claims.
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
